# US-01.1 — Provision the Google Cloud environment with one command

|                  |                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-01 Foundation & Environment](../epics/EPIC-01-foundation-environment.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                             |
| **Estimate**     | 2                                                                              |
| **Status**       | Done (gap)                                                                     |
| **Owning agent** | `cloud-deployer`                                                               |
| **Files**        | [setup_gcp.sh](../../../setup_gcp.sh), `.env`                                  |

## User story

**As a** developer joining the project,
**I want** a single script that provisions every Google Cloud resource and writes my local configuration,
**so that** I can go from a fresh clone to a working environment without reading cloud documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — APIs enabled**
Given a project with no APIs enabled,
when I run `./setup_gcp.sh`,
then aiplatform, run, storage, bigquery, pubsub, and firestore are all enabled.

**AC2 — Resources created in the mandated region**
Given the bucket, topic, and Firestore database do not exist,
when the script runs,
then all three are created in `asia-southeast1`.

**AC3 — Idempotent**
Given every resource already exists,
when I run the script a second time,
then it completes successfully and creates nothing new.

**AC4 — Configuration written**
Given the script completes,
then `.env` contains `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION`, `GCS_BUCKET_NAME`, `PUBSUB_TOPIC_ID`, and `MODEL_ID` with non-empty values.

**AC5 — Frontend origin configured**
Given the script completes,
then `.env` also contains `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, so the API's CORS configuration has a value to read in [EPIC-05](../epics/EPIC-05-api-service.md).

## Tasks

- [x] Authenticate gcloud and Application Default Credentials
- [x] Discover or prompt for the project ID
- [x] Enable the six required APIs
- [x] Create bucket, topic, and Firestore database when absent
- [x] Write the `.env` heredoc
- [ ] Add `ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8501` to the `.env` heredoc
- [ ] Correct the `setup_gcp.zsh` reference in [Epics_Stories.md](../../../Epics_Stories.md) — the real filename is `setup_gcp.sh`

## Current state

The script works and is safe to re-run. Two gaps remain:

| Gap                                       | Impact                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` never written to `.env` | EPIC-05 falls back to a hardcoded default; the deployed dashboard will hit CORS errors |
| Execution docs say `source setup_gcp.zsh` | That file does not exist — a new developer's first command fails                       |

## Test cases

This story provisions live infrastructure, so it is verified by the `gcp-environment-doctor` skill rather than by pytest.

| Case                          | Expectation                                        |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `doctor.py` after a clean run | All environment checks pass                        |
| `.env` key presence           | All six variables present and non-empty            |
| Second consecutive run        | Exit code 0, no new resources                      |
| Region check                  | `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION` is exactly `asia-southeast1` |

## Definition of done

`python3 .github/skills/gcp-environment-doctor/scripts/doctor.py` reports every check green on a machine that has only cloned the repository and run the script once.

## Notes

The script mutates cloud infrastructure and requires an interactive login. The `guard-cloud-commands` hook deliberately asks before any agent runs it — run it yourself rather than delegating.
